chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: "Among the traditions of the Prophets are al-istinja' (ritual cleansing after relieving oneself) and al-khitam (circumcision)."

key_terms.اَلْاِسْتِنْجَاءُ: Ritual cleansing of the private parts after relieving oneself
key_terms.اَلْمُرْسَلِينَ: The Prophets (specifically those sent with divine laws)

ai.seo_question: What are the two main traditions of the prophets mentioned in this hadith regarding purity and circumcision?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration in the chapter of childbirth and postpartum rites, linking physical hygiene to the innate nature (fitrah) of the prophets. By classifying istinja' and circumcision as 'sunan al-mursalun' (traditions of the sent ones), the hadith elevates these acts from mere legal obligations to enduring prophetic customs, reinforcing their spiritual and physical significance in Shia jurisprudence.
